identity.name: npm Supply-Chain Compromise on a Linux Developer Endpoint — Preinstall-Hook Credential Theft via a Phantom-Squatted Package
identity.summary: A malicious npm package (reached via an AI-hallucinated / slopsquatted name) runs a preinstall lifecycle hook that spawns node, harvests developer credential files, base64-stages and archives them, and dead-drops the archive — all executed FOR REAL against a staged decoy developer $HOME on a bare Ubuntu endpoint.
identity.description: Built from Unit 42's 'The npm Threat Landscape' research (https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/), with the phantom-squatting / slopsquatting entry vector drawn from Unit 42's 'Phantom Squatting' work (https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/phantom-squatting-hallucinated-web-domains/). The npm research documents malicious packages whose package.json carries a lifecycle hook — "scripts":{"preinstall":"node setup.mjs"} (also seen "preinstall":"bun run index.js") — so that `npm install` detonates attacker code, which on Linux reads ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.ssh/keys, .git/config, ~/.npmrc, .npmrc, .env, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.claude/mcp.json, ~/.claude.json and ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json, encodes and stages the loot, and exfiltrates it to a GitHub dead-drop (helloworm00/hello-world) and C2 (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43). Unlike a SAFE-MODE echo, CortexSim EXECUTES this chain for real: it stages a fake $HOME at /var/tmp/.koi010-victim populated with literal CORTEXSIM-DECOY credential files, builds a real decoy package carrying a preinstall hook, runs `npm install --ignore-scripts=false` so the hook really spawns `node setup.mjs`, runs a real `node harvest.mjs` that reads the decoy credential files, base64-stages and tars the result, and dead-drops it locally — every read and write guarded to the /var/tmp decoy tree, never the operator's real home. The phantom-squatting stage runs a real `npm install` of a never-registered, AI-hallucinated package name pointed at a non-resolving .invalid registry, producing process and failed-resolution telemetry with no egress. Detections anchor on the npm/node install causality chain (actor_causality_id and the npm/node image-name set), never on a username, because the Causality Group Owner is the node install process. Declared (scored) expectations are only what is reachable without deploying custom content or putting a sink in path: the built-in 'uncommon Linux shell command execution' analytic on the npm->node setup.mjs detonation, the behavioural credential-access verdict on the install-hook descendant's multi-credential read, validation XQL (reachable by construction) for the package create / slopsquat-install visibility / base64 stage / archive create, and correlation CR-KOI-0010 whose terminal term is the LOCAL archive create (so it closes on the endpoint). Hunting content, deliberately NOT declared as an expectation: the fleet-wide phantom-squat / slopsquat resolution hunt, the archive-egress XQL (points at the non-resolving cortexsim-koi010.invalid placeholder and needs a firewall/sink in path), and the precise path-keyed credential BIOCs. Documented but NOT exercised, because it is GCP control-plane and not endpoint-executable: Unit 42's 'Pickle in the Middle' Vertex AI model-upload hijack — cataloged here as the cloud-plane sibling of this endpoint supply-chain chain (covered by Cortex AI-SPM / Cortex Cloud, not the XDR agent), never declared as a firing expectation. IOC note: the setup.mjs / execution.js / bw_setup.js payload SHA256s are published in the report's IOC table; this card carries their filenames and the campaign's network/dead-drop indicators with source_url to the npm post, and a DC should paste the exact hashes from the live report when deploying hash IOCs.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-KOI-010 — npm supply-chain developer-endpoint credential theft, executed for real against a staged decoy $HOME (/var/tmp/.koi010-victim) via the npm preinstall lifecycle hook.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the Linux developer endpoint so per-process causality telemetry reaches xdr_data.

payload.code:
# NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE SCENARIO: scenarios/koi/sim-koi-010-npm-supply-chain-dev-endpoint-credential-theft.yml is the only supported delivery path. It stages the decoy $HOME, decoy credential stores and the malicious package, then detonates the preinstall hook, harvests, stages, archives and dead-drops — every step guarded to /var/tmp/.koi010-victim. This snippet only sketches the preinstall-hook mechanism.
set -eu
export HOME=/var/tmp/.koi010-victim
PKG="$HOME/.cache/koi010-pkg"
# package.json carries: "scripts": { "preinstall": "node setup.mjs" }
cd "$PKG" && npm install --ignore-scripts=false --no-audit --no-fund --no-package-lock
# the hook spawns node, which reads the decoy ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.claude/mcp.json ...

input_variables.name: VICTIM_HOME
input_variables.description: Staged decoy $HOME; the chain never touches the operator's real home.

expected_artifacts.description: package.json declaring an npm preinstall lifecycle hook (node setup.mjs), created under the decoy package directory.
node spawned by the npm install lifecycle hook running setup.mjs.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: actor_process_image_name = "npm" and action_process_image_name = "node" and action_process_image_command_line contains "setup.mjs"

expected_artifacts.description: Decoy developer credential files read by the install-hook descendant.
base64 encoding the harvested credential bundle under the npm/node install lineage.
tar archive of the staged credential bundle (exfil.tgz) under the decoy tree.

cleanup.code:
pkill -f '/var/tmp/.koi010-victim/' 2>/dev/null || true
rm -rf /var/tmp/.koi010-victim
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-KOI-010 cleanup complete.'

biocs.name: KOI-010 Multi Credential File Read Under npm Node CGO
biocs.description: Three or more distinct developer credential-named files (SSH private keys, .npmrc token, AWS credentials, .env, agent MCP config, .git/config) are read in one window by a process in the npm/node install causality chain. An install-hook descendant that reads this set is stealing, not building. Card-only deployable content: not declared as a scenario expectation, so a tenant without it deployed is never scored a MISS; the equivalent behavioural ABIOC is the declared, agent-raised twin.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_OPEN, ENUM.FILE_READ)
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("npm", "node")
| filter action_file_path contains_any (".ssh/id_rsa", ".ssh/id_ed25519", ".npmrc", ".aws/credentials", ".env", ".claude/mcp.json", ".claude.json", ".kiro/settings/mcp.json", ".git/config", ".git-credentials")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as secret_files_read, values(action_file_path) as paths by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_image_name
| filter secret_files_read >= 3
| fields agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_image_name, paths, secret_files_read

biocs.name: KOI-010 Credential Archive Egress From npm Install Lineage
biocs.description: A process in the npm/node install causality chain uploads bytes to the campaign's dead-drop / C2 hosts (or the lab's non-resolving placeholder). biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("npm", "node", "curl")
| filter action_external_hostname in ("cortexsim-koi010.invalid", "audit.checkmarx.cx") or dst_action_external_hostname in ("cortexsim-koi010.invalid", "audit.checkmarx.cx")
| filter action_total_upload > 0
| comp sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, action_external_hostname

| fields agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, action_external_hostname, bytes_out

abiocs.name: KOI-010 Uncommon Shell Command Execution Under npm Install Hook Lineage
abiocs.description: Behavioral-ML deviation (the built-in 'uncommon Linux shell command execution' analytic, scoped to causality): the npm/node install process spawns a child exec that is anomalous for the npm/node install causality on this host — node running an install-time script (setup.mjs) out of the preinstall hook. Package installs rarely spawn arbitrary interpreters; a first-seen package doing it at install time is the lifecycle-hook detonation shape.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("npm", "node", "npm-cli.js") or actor_process_image_name in ("npm", "node")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("setup.mjs", "preinstall", "postinstall", "bun run index.js")
| comp count() as uncommon_execs, values(action_process_image_command_line) as child_cmdlines by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter uncommon_execs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, child_cmdlines, uncommon_execs
abiocs.causality_anchor: The npm/node install process (Causality Group Owner) and its causality_actor_process_instance_id; the deviation is an uncommon install-time exec (node setup.mjs from the preinstall hook) against the baseline of package installs that spawn no interpreters.

An install hook that reads this set is harvesting, not resolving dependencies.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE

| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as secret_files_read, values(action_file_path) as paths by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter secret_files_read >= 3
| fields agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id, paths, secret_files_read
abiocs.causality_anchor: The npm/node install process (Causality Group Owner); the deviation is an install-hook descendant reading a multi-credential set in one window against the baseline of installs that read only package metadata.

correlation_rules.name: npm Supply-Chain Credential Theft — Preinstall-Hook Detonation, Credential Harvest, Obfuscated Stage and Archive
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(KOI-010 Uncommon Shell Command Execution Under npm Install Hook Lineage) FOLLOWED_BY ABIOC(KOI-010 npm Install Hook Descendant Reads Multiple Developer Credential Files) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(KOI-010 Credentials Read And base64 Staged Under npm Install Lineage) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(KOI-010 Credential Archive Created Under npm Install Lineage) — all stitched by shared agent_hostname and actor_causality_id (CGO = the npm/node install process) so the lifecycle-hook detonation, multi-credential read, obfuscated staging and local archive collapse into ONE npm-supply-chain incident. The chain closes on the endpoint: its terminal term is the local archive create, not the egress, so the rule fires in a lab with no authorised sink and no firewall in path.

CortexSim does not reproduce it; it is cataloged here as the cloud-plane sibling of this endpoint supply-chain chain, covered by Cortex AI-SPM / Cortex Cloud rather than the XDR agent, and is never declared as a firing expectation.

threat_scenarios.name: npm Supply-Chain Compromise on a Developer Endpoint — Phantom-Squat to Credential Theft
threat_scenarios.description: Detect a malicious npm package end to end on a Linux developer endpoint: a hallucinated / slopsquatted install, a preinstall lifecycle hook that detonates node, a multi-credential harvest, an obfuscated local stage and archive, stitched into one causality-aware incident, with a dead-drop egress leg available for hunting when a firewall is in path.

threat_steps.objective: The slopsquat install attempt is visible and the preinstall-hook detonation fires under the npm/node install causality chain.
preconditions: Linux developer endpoint with the Cortex agent and node/npm installed.
steps: Stage the decoy developer workspace, credential stores and the malicious package.
Run the phantom-squat `npm install` of the AI-hallucinated package name against a non-resolving registry.
Run `npm install` on the malicious package so the preinstall hook detonates node setup.mjs.
success_criteria: XQL `KOI-010 Phantom Squatting Hallucinated Package Install Attempt` returns the slopsquat install process.
ABIOC `KOI-010 Uncommon Shell Command Execution Under npm Install Hook Lineage` fires on the preinstall-hook detonation.
XQL `KOI-010 Malicious npm Package With Preinstall Lifecycle Hook Created On Developer Endpoint` returns the package.json/setup.mjs create.

threat_steps.objective: The credential harvest, obfuscated stage and archive fire and correlate into one incident on the endpoint.
preconditions: TS-KOI-010A executed within the correlation window.
steps: Run `node harvest.mjs` to read the decoy credential files.
base64-stage and tar the harvested bundle.
Dead-drop the archive locally and emit a hunt-only egress beacon at the non-resolving placeholder.
success_criteria: ABIOC `KOI-010 npm Install Hook Descendant Reads Multiple Developer Credential Files` fires.
XQL `KOI-010 Credentials Read And base64 Staged Under npm Install Lineage` returns the base64 stage.
XQL `KOI-010 Credential Archive Created Under npm Install Lineage` returns the exfil.tgz create.
Correlation `CR-KOI-0010` raises exactly one npm-supply-chain incident. Its terminal term is the local archive create, so it fires on the endpoint alone: no sink and no firewall in path are required.

Not a criterion: the fleet-wide phantom-squat hunt and the archive-egress query carry `purpose: hunt`. The scenario declares neither as an expectation, so a sink-less run seeds nothing for them and scores neither a pass nor a fail against them.

preventive_controls: Install dependencies with lifecycle scripts disabled by default (npm config set ignore-scripts true; opt in per-trusted-package) so a preinstall/postinstall hook cannot detonate on `npm install`.

Gate developer package installs through an internal registry proxy that blocks unknown / newly-published / typosquatted / AI-hallucinated names, and alert on any install of a package first seen in the fleet.
Keep long-lived credentials out of developer home directories: use short-lived tokens, a credential helper and hardware-backed SSH keys so an install-hook file read yields nothing reusable.

Pin and vet AI coding-assistant package suggestions against the registry before install, to close the slopsquatting / phantom-squatting vector where a hallucinated name is pre-registered by an attacker.
detection_engineering: Anchor on actor_causality_id and the npm/node image-name set, never on a username: the npm/node install process is the Causality Group Owner and every later stage is its descendant.
Treat an install lineage that spawns node/base64/tar or reads SSH keys, .npmrc, cloud credentials or agent MCP config as the signal; none is part of a normal dependency install.
Require three or more distinct credential-named files read in one window by the install chain before alerting on credential theft, to keep a single settings read quiet.
Keep time windows as timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < N and join on actor_causality_id so the stage/archive/egress legs stitch to the same install process.

Pair the endpoint chain with NGFW egress to a non-registry destination when a firewall is in path, and with Cortex Cloud Code / AI-SPM for the package-manifest and Vertex-AI model-upload surfaces this endpoint chain does not cover.
